_comment: Fault-to-product matrix. Links are built as Amazon search URLs with ?tag=<NEXT_PUBLIC_AMAZON_ASSOCIATES_TAG> (placeholder YOUR-TAG-20). After Associates approval, paste each product's ASIN into 'asin' to switch to a direct /dp/ link.

over_the_top.title: Over-the-Top / Out-to-In Path (Slice)
over_the_top.why: Your hands move out toward the ball at the start of the downswing, which steepens the shaft and swings the club across the ball, the classic slice and pull pattern.

drill.name: Headcover Gate + Pump Drill
steps: Place a headcover just outside and behind the ball (toward your trail foot).
Swing to the top, then pump halfway down, feeling your trail elbow drop into your trail hip.
Swing through without hitting the headcover. 3 sets of 10 slow-motion reps.

products.name: Power Angle Pro
products.blurb: Wrist-and-forearm trainer that trains the shallowing and lag that cures an over-the-top move.
products.searchQuery: Power Angle Pro golf training aid

products.name: Tour Striker PlaneMate 2.0
products.blurb: Resistance-band trainer that pulls you onto plane and shallows the downswing.

products.name: Swing Doctor Golf Swing Trainer
products.blurb: Arm-connection trainer that keeps the trail elbow tucked from the top.

early_extension.title: Early Extension (Hips Thrust Toward the Ball)
early_extension.why: Your hips move toward the ball before impact, which removes the room your arms need and causes blocks, hooks, and thin or fat contact.

drill.name: Chair / Wall Butt Drill
steps: Set up with your backside just touching a wall or chair behind you.
Make slow swings keeping your trail glute on the wall in the backswing and your lead glute on it through impact.
Work up to half-speed swings with a 7-iron. 20 reps per session.

products.name: theTILTSTICK
products.blurb: Clips to your belt and gives instant feedback when your hips stand up early.

products.name: Alignment Sticks (3-pack)
products.blurb: Stick one in the ground behind your hips as a posture reference for every rep.

loss_of_posture.title: Loss of Spine Angle (Standing Up)
loss_of_posture.why: Your spine angle gets more upright between address and impact. That changes the low point of your swing and usually pairs with early extension.

drill.name: Hold-the-Tilt Pump Drill
steps: Hold a club across your chest at address and note your forward bend.
Rotate back and through, keeping your chest pointing at the ground until well past impact.
Film a down-the-line rep every 10 swings to check that your head stays inside the box.

products.name: theTILTSTICK
products.blurb: Gives direct posture feedback so you can keep your tilt through impact.

products.name: Alignment Sticks (3-pack)
products.blurb: Use one as a spine-angle reference along your back in slow-motion reps.

sway.title: Hip Sway / Poor Weight Shift
sway.why: Your hips slide sideways instead of rotating, or they fail to move toward the target by impact, so your low point and strike stay inconsistent.

drill.name: Alignment-Stick Hip Gate
steps: Push an alignment stick into the ground just outside your trail hip.
Turn back without touching the stick, feeling pressure on the inside of your trail foot.
Bump your lead hip toward the target to start down, then hold a balanced finish for 3 seconds.

products.name: Alignment Sticks with Adjustable Holder
products.blurb: Ground holder makes a vertical hip gate that stops the slide.

products.name: Alignment Sticks (3-pack)
products.blurb: Basic fiberglass sticks for the hip gate and alignment work.

casting.title: Casting / Early Release (Flipping)
casting.why: Your hands are behind the ball at impact, a sign that you throw the club early and lose lag. You lose distance, and contact gets thin or fat with high, weak shots.

drill.name: Pump-and-Hold Lag Drill
steps: Swing to the top, then pull the butt of the grip down to your trail thigh while keeping your wrist hinge.
Stop there for 2 seconds, then finish with your hands ahead of the ball and the shaft leaning toward the target.
Hit half-shots with the goal of a divot after the ball. 3 sets of 10.

products.name: theHANGER
products.blurb: Shaft attachment that teaches a flat lead wrist and forward shaft lean at impact.

products.name: Anti-Flip Stick
products.blurb: Gives instant feedback the moment your lead wrist breaks down through the ball.

products.name: Lag Shot 7 Iron
products.blurb: Whippy-shaft 7-iron that only flushes when you hold lag and sequence correctly.
products.searchQuery: Lag Shot 7 iron golf training aid

chicken_wing.title: Chicken Wing (Bent Lead Arm Through Impact)
chicken_wing.why: Your lead elbow collapses after impact instead of extending, which shortens the arc and leaves the face open.

drill.name: Towel-Under-Arms Connection Drill
steps: Tuck a towel under both armpits.
Make 3/4 swings, keeping the towel in place until your hands pass your lead thigh.
Feel both arms extend toward the target after impact. 20 reps.

products.name: Tour Striker Smart Ball
products.blurb: Inflatable ball you hold between your forearms to keep your arms connected and extended through impact.

products.name: Swing Doctor Golf Swing Trainer
products.blurb: Keeps your arms working together so your lead elbow doesn't fold.

bent_lead_arm.title: Bent Lead Arm at the Top
bent_lead_arm.why: Your lead arm folds at the top, which narrows the arc and makes the downswing harder to time.

drill.name: Wide Takeaway Drill
steps: Hold your lead arm straight but not locked, and push the club away low and wide.
Stop at the top when your lead arm can no longer stay extended.
Make 10 lead-arm-only swings, then 10 full swings with the same width.

products.name: Tour Striker Smart Ball
products.blurb: Keeps the triangle between your arms and chest intact through the backswing.

products.name: Tour Striker PlaneMate 2.0
products.blurb: Band resistance encourages a wide, on-plane backswing.

poor_tempo.title: Tempo / Rhythm Off
poor_tempo.why: Tour players average about a 3:1 backswing-to-downswing time ratio. A rushed or sluggish ratio throws off your sequencing and timing.

drill.name: 3-to-1 Metronome Drill
steps: Set a metronome app to about 70 to 80 BPM.
Start the takeaway on beat 1, reach the top on beat 3, and hit impact on beat 4.
10 swings with the metronome, then 10 without it, keeping the same count in your head.

products.name: Orange Whip Trainer
products.blurb: Weighted, flexible trainer that forces a smooth transition and good rhythm.

products.name: Lag Shot Driver / 7 Iron
products.blurb: Whippy shaft punishes a rushed transition, so it rewards good tempo.

setup_alignment.title: Setup: Posture, Stance & Alignment
setup_alignment.why: Your setup (stance width or forward tilt) is outside the usual range. Every swing fault downstream starts at address.

drill.name: Two-Stick Setup Station
steps: Lay one alignment stick on your target line and one on your foot line, parallel.
Set your feet about shoulder-width for a mid-iron and tilt from the hips until your arms hang under your shoulders.
Check the setup on video from both views before every practice session.

products.name: Fiberglass Alignment Sticks (3-pack)
products.blurb: The most-used practice aid for building a repeatable setup and aim.

head_movement.title: Excess Head Movement
head_movement.why: Your head moves a lot between address and impact, which shifts the bottom of your arc and makes centered contact harder.

drill.name: Shadow / Stick Head Check
steps: Set up with the sun behind you, or an alignment stick pointed at your head on video.
Make swings keeping your head's shadow within a ball-width until impact.
Let your head release toward the target only after impact.

products.name: Alignment Sticks with Adjustable Holder
products.blurb: Set a vertical stick next to your head as a stability reference.
